Everyone here understands that Anon is a completely ambiguous "group," right?

lulsec was a group of hackers that had the brilliant idea to use the common activist as cover for their protests, while simultaneously inspiring said activists off their respective couches.

Eventually lulsec dissolved somewhat, because they realized putting a name on their group just gave the MSM a handle with which to slam hacktivists.

Years later, Anonymous is still thrown around, but it only persists as a pseudonym for "persons unknown." The media saying "who is this hacker called anonymous" is pretty close to us folks asking who the Illuminati's leader is.

Outside of the Anon videos where threats and demands are made, and these threats are then backed up, I'd venture to say the actual power-players behind lulsec have long-since distanced themselves from this throwaway term.

My point being, everyone is anonymous until they sign their name at the bottom of their message, so a twitter post (while accurate in this instance) is extremely unlikely to have anything even indirectly to do with the real players that used the throwaways "lulsec" and "anonymous."

we need to revise the rules..

I'm in the IRC to talk this over again, please stop by!

So the results of the poll, image backup, indicate we generally want to keep images. However we cant ignore the proportion who don't want them, because it was still a large percentage. So we need a balance.

Making a judgement based on the comments in the poll thread , as well as previous threads posted , it's clear we need to rethink the rules.

So, from this point forward image posts, gifs, webm's and video clips all need to have:

Clear, concise titles, that accurately reflect the content

This means no pun titles and no DAE posts. The title should be a short description of the post and nothing else. Many of you may not agree with this, but this acts as a compromise. This is a very good example that I saw recently. An example of the type of thing not allowed can be seen here and here.

This is rule 2 and will be enforced heavily

Flairs in the title to denote the name of the game,

For example [GTAV]. Submissions without these flairs will be removed. The added benefit to flairs, is the ease to find posts through search.

No memes

This one is already a rule (#4) but I want to reinforce it. We will delete every meme post. /v/gamingmemes or /v/gamingpics may be a good alternative.

The original title (wherever possible)

This mainly applies to videos, so trailers, gameplays, interviews etc. If It isn't possible, follow the rule above.

The original source (wherever possible)

If a video has a direct link, post it, don't link to a site with an embedded video. Extends to images. Try to use veuwer when uploading images.

No links to illegal torrents or other illegal downloads/content

This means no cracked games or copyrighted material unfairly distributed.

You can however link to torrents in cases where developers may be distributing their games via this medium (or other software etc)

Please also remember to mark all NSFW posts appropriately (Rule #9)

I'll be lenient for the first few weeks, while people grow accustomed to these revisions. The rule is now in the sidebar and will link to this thread, so people are able to see it in more detail. If people have an issue with these rules, they should take into account we have decided as a community.

So far content has been great and there are lots of discussions. These new rules should help maintain that and I ask that we try and post images, videos etc that promote discussions. Engaging people is the best way to keep a community fresh. We will see how the posts continue over the coming months and again revise the rules if content is slipping.

With these changes we still welcome all content, however you should be aware of the existence of relevant subverses.

Namely: /v/gamingpics /v/gameart /v/gameclips /v/gamingmemes /v/gamedeals /v/randomactsofgaming /v/gamernews

I'm also currently thinking about weekly threads (possible two days a week). Saturday could be a 'Saturday-Share' day where anything goes, memes, devs plugging games, pics etc. Anything within relevance and legal bounds. 'Topic-Tuesdays' could be there for a weekly discussion thread, which I'd leave up into Wednesday. Let me know your thoughts below please!

We also recently created /v/ideasforgaming where you can share your thoughts and interact with me more easily if you have any concerns. I'm also always lurking in the subverse's IRC, so I'm around for a chat or to address any concerns :)
